text: A store owner kept losing money, and his fix cost exactly one cent.
Back then, you paid one dollar, and the clerk didn't need to give change.
So he just slipped your dollar into his pocket.
No receipt. No record. Nobody knew.
So, the story goes, the owner changed every price to ninety-nine cents.
Now the clerk owed you a penny.
And the only place to get a penny was the register, which rings a bell and records the sale.
Every sale counted. The stealing stopped.
But today stores have cameras and card machines, and the ninety-nine never left.
You see, your brain reads a price from left to right, and it decides on the first number.
Two ninety-nine feels like two dollars, not three.
So the ninety-nine was made to catch the clerk, and now it catches you.
